title: Dengue fever (mosquito-borne viral illness)

items: Dengue is a viral illness spread by mosquito bites in tropical areas.
It usually starts 4 to 7 days after a bite, and can get worse as the fever falls.
Sudden fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, and body and joint aches.
NS1 antigen test, best in the first 5 days of fever.
Dengue antibody tests later in the illness.
Repeated blood counts and haematocrit (the share of blood that is red cells), since platelets can fall.
Your doctor will advise on treatment and close monitoring.
Ask your doctor which pain or fever relief is safe for you.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Drink plenty of fluids, and rest.
Use mosquito protection to stop further spread.
Your team may repeat blood counts over the next days, because the danger period is when the fever falls.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Persistent vomiting (3 or more times in 1 hour, or 4 or more in 6 hours)
Belly pain, lethargy or restlessness, or bleeding from the gums or nose
A rising haematocrit (share of red cells in the blood) on repeat tests
